title: Arjuna bows before the bow
hook: a disguised archer walks around the bow and bows before he lifts it
carry: pradakshina: honor what's sacred before you begin

segments.voice: Yesterday: Karna at the bow, one sentence from the princess, and a glance at the sun. Your line: Surya, the sun, sees what the arena can't.
screen: `SURYA, THE SUN, SEES WHAT THE ARENA CAN'T.`

segments.voice: The kings have failed. Karna has put down the bow. The arena goes quiet. From the benches where the brahmins sit, a young man stands up, dressed like any brahmin student. The brahmins around him murmur. Some are alarmed: where famous kings have failed, what's a brahmin going to do, except make the rest of us look foolish? Others look at his arms and the way he carries himself, and say: let him go.
screen: `THE ARENA GOES QUIET.` → `A BRAHMIN STANDS UP.`

segments.voice: It's Arjuna, in disguise. He walks up to the bow and around it, the text says, bows his head to Shiva, the giver of boons, and remembers Krishna. Then he picks it up. In a moment the bow is strung. He shoots, and the mark falls to the ground. The arena erupts. Flowers fall from the sky, the text says, and Draupadi comes toward him and places her garland on him. The kings are furious that a nameless brahmin has taken the prize, and they rise to fight; Bhima tears up a tree and stands beside his brother. But go back to that pause before the bow. The best archer alive, in front of every king, stops, walks around the thing he's about to use, and bows. Hindus still do exactly this. Walking around something holy, keeping it on your right, is called pradakshina: people circle the shrine at a temple, the tulsi plant at home, and at a wedding the couple circle the sacred fire. And the bow before the work is everywhere: a dancer touches the floor before she dances, a musician touches the instrument, a child who drops a book touches it, then touches their forehead. The teaching underneath: what you're about to use isn't only a tool. Honor first, then act. Arjuna's strength comes after his bow.
screen: `HE WALKS AROUND THE BOW AND BOWS.` · `THE MARK FALLS.` · `DRAUPADI'S GARLAND.` · `PRADAKSHINA: CIRCLE WHAT'S HOLY.` · then, large: `HONOR FIRST, THEN ACT.`

segments.voice: Before something today asks a lot of you, do what Arjuna did, and what Hindu families do every day. Stop in front of it. If you pray, fold your hands and remember God by whatever name your family uses; if there's a home shrine or a tulsi plant nearby, some families walk around it once, keeping it on the right. If you don't pray, simply stand still and bow your head to the work for one slow breath. Then begin.
Draupadi's swayamvara, the bride's own choosing. Today, a disguised archer honors the bow before he lifts it, and wins.
Your line: pradakshina: honor what's sacred before you begin. Arjuna bowed first; the strength came after. Until tomorrow.
